title: Capstone Seminar in Statistics

gradingBreakdown.component: Writing memos and one presentation (unweighted average, ~8 assignments)

weeklyTopics: ~8 case studies, each covering roughly 3 lectures of background/statistical issues followed by a 10-day writing assignment

Case study domains include human health, social/behavioral science, and natural science (e.g. NHANES, mortality, actigraphy, RLMS, COVID testing/mortality data, per the shared course case-studies repo)
Statistical methods introduced per case study: GLMs, GEE, mixed/multilevel regression, survival analysis, dimension reduction, time series
Technical writing: framing a research question, methods justification, findings/interpretation memos
One in-class student presentation per student (4-5 slides, 5-minute talk)
workloadNotes: Capstone seminar for 2nd-year Applied Statistics/Data Science master's students; ~8 individual case-study writing assignments (2-3 page memos) graded on a 4-part rubric (focus, methods/approach, writing/organization, findings/interpretation, 25 points each), plus one student presentation; course grade is an unweighted average of all assignment scores; no exams; code is not submitted or graded.
prerequisitesText: Master's-level courses in probability, theoretical statistics, regression analysis, and multivariate statistics.
